key_concepts: Earthquakes occur when rock under stress breaks within Earth
The focus is the underground point where rock breaks
The epicenter is the surface point directly above the focus
Magnitude measures the size or amplitude of seismic waves
Intensity measures the strength of shaking experienced
Seismic waves are vibrations generated by earthquakes and propagated through Earth
Normal faults involve the hanging wall moving downward in tensional settings
Reverse faults involve the hanging wall moving upward in compressional settings
Strike-slip faults involve horizontal sliding of tectonic plates past each other
Earthquake damage depends on magnitude and distance from the earthquake
PHIVOLCS FaultFinder identifies nearby active fault traces and supports earthquake risk as
Underwater earthquakes may or may not generate tsunamis
